title: Food Science B 2027: the Science of Dairy
summary: Food Science 2027 is a dairy event. Teams make ice cream, separate curds and churn butter, keep a notebook of nine experiments, and sit a written exam the manual scopes to dairy topics only. This course covers that exam topic by topic, and the chemistry behind each of the three lab tasks.
objectives: Explain milk as an emulsion of fat in a protein and sugar solution, and predict what acid, heat and agitation each do to it
Identify the structures and bonds of the sugars, fats and proteins of dairy foods, and the reactions that build and break them
Compute a freezing point depression and explain why the ice cream task needs salt
Read a Nutrition Facts label, apply RDA and Daily Value correctly, and name the deficiency each dairy nutrient prevents
Distinguish lactose intolerance from milk allergy by mechanism, and compare non-dairy alternatives honestly
Design a dairy experiment with one independent variable and report its result with units and an error statement

units.title: What Milk Is
units.summary: Milk is an emulsion of fat in an aqueous solution of protein, sugar and minerals. Every task and every exam topic in this event follows from that sentence.
objectives: Name the components of milk and the phase each one occupies
Explain why milk is opaque and why cream rises

lessons.title: The Four Fractions of Milk
lessons.objective: List the fat, protein, carbohydrate, mineral and water fractions of whole milk with approximate percentages, and state which are dissolved, which are suspended and which are emulsified.

lessons.title: The Fat Globule and Why Cream Rises
lessons.objective: Describe the milk fat globule and its membrane, and explain in terms of density why cream separates from unhomogenized milk and what homogenization does to stop it.

lessons.title: Casein: the Micelle That Holds Milk Together
lessons.objective: Describe the casein micelle, name the caseins it contains, and explain what holds it dispersed at milk's natural pH.

lessons.title: Whey: the Protein That Stays Behind
lessons.objective: Distinguish whey proteins from caseins by how each responds to acid and to heat, and say which fraction drains through the cheesecloth.

units.title: The Molecules: Sugars, Fats and Proteins
units.summary: The manual asks for the chemical structure of sugars, starches, fats and proteins, and for the organic reactions that build and break fats.
objectives: Draw or describe the bonds that build each macromolecule class
Classify a fat as saturated or unsaturated from its structure

lessons.title: Lactose: a Disaccharide of Glucose and Galactose
lessons.objective: Identify lactose as a disaccharide, name its two monosaccharides and the glycosidic bond joining them, and explain why it must be split before absorption.

lessons.title: From Sugars to Starches
lessons.objective: Compare monosaccharides, disaccharides and polysaccharides, and explain why starch is a storage molecule while lactose is a transport sugar.

lessons.title: Triglycerides: Three Fatty Acids on a Glycerol
lessons.objective: Describe a triglyceride as three fatty acids esterified to glycerol, and identify the ester linkage in a structure.

lessons.title: Saturated, Unsaturated and Trans
lessons.objective: Decide from a structure or description whether a fatty acid is saturated, unsaturated or trans, and predict its melting behaviour and packing.

lessons.title: Making and Breaking a Fat
lessons.objective: Write what esterification joins and what hydrolysis and saponification break, and say which of these happens when a fat goes rancid.

lessons.title: Proteins: Amino Acids and the Peptide Bond
lessons.objective: Describe how amino acids join through peptide bonds, name the four levels of protein structure, and identify which levels denaturation destroys.

lessons.title: Essential Fats, Amino Acids and Why 'Essential' Means One Thing
lessons.objective: Explain what makes a fatty acid, an amino acid or a vitamin 'essential', and name the essential nutrients dairy foods supply.

units.title: Emulsification
units.summary: Milk is an emulsion, butter is an inverted one, and ice cream is a foam sitting on top of both.
objectives: Explain how an emulsifier stabilises two phases that do not mix
Say what churning does to an emulsion

lessons.title: Oil, Water and the Molecule That Joins Them
lessons.objective: Define an emulsion and explain how an amphipathic emulsifier stabilises it, using the hydrophilic and hydrophobic ends explicitly.

lessons.title: Churning Cream Into Butter
lessons.objective: Explain what shaking cream does to the fat globule membranes, and describe the phase inversion from fat-in-water to water-in-fat that produces butter and buttermilk.

lessons.title: Colloids, Suspensions and Solutions
lessons.objective: Classify each component of milk as a solution, a colloid or a suspension, and explain why milk scatters light.

units.title: Coagulation: Curds, Cheese and Cooking
units.summary: The curd mass task is an acid coagulation, and the manual also asks how cooking changes dairy foods chemically.
objectives: Predict what acid does to casein and what heat does to whey
Explain the chemistry behind the curd mass lab task

lessons.title: Why Vinegar Makes Curds
lessons.objective: Explain how adding acid lowers pH toward casein's isoelectric point, and why the micelle then aggregates into curd.

lessons.title: The Other Way: Rennet and Chymosin
lessons.objective: Contrast enzymatic coagulation by chymosin with acid coagulation, and say which one cheesemaking usually uses.

lessons.title: What Cooking Does to Milk
lessons.objective: Describe what heating does to whey proteins, to lactose and to milk's surface, and name the skin, the scald and the browning by their chemistry.

lessons.title: Cultured Dairy: Bacteria That Make Acid
lessons.objective: Explain how lactic acid fermentation converts lactose to lactic acid, and how that produces yogurt, buttermilk and kefir.

lessons.title: Probiotics: Live Cultures and What They Claim
lessons.objective: State what makes an organism a probiotic, name the genera used in dairy foods, and distinguish a live culture from a pasteurized product.

units.title: Freezing Point Depression and the Ice Cream Task
units.summary: The ice cream task works because salt on ice makes a bath colder than pure ice can be. This unit is the physical chemistry the manual names.
objectives: Compute a freezing point depression from molality
Explain why the salt goes in the OUTER bag

lessons.title: Properties That Count Particles, Not Kinds
lessons.objective: Define a colligative property and explain why freezing point depression depends on the number of dissolved particles rather than what they are.

lessons.title: Working Out How Cold the Bath Gets
lessons.objective: Use the freezing point depression relationship with molality and the van 't Hoff factor to compute the depression for a salt-ice bath, showing units.

lessons.title: Why Salt and Ice Get Colder Than Ice
lessons.objective: Explain, using enthalpy of fusion and the energy the melting ice takes from its surroundings, why an ice-salt bath falls below zero degrees Celsius.

lessons.title: Ice Cream Is a Foam, an Emulsion and a Suspension at Once
lessons.objective: Describe ice cream as ice crystals, fat globules and air cells in a freeze-concentrated solution, and explain what agitation during freezing controls.

units.title: Pasteurization and Preservation
units.summary: How dairy foods are made safe and made to last, and what each process costs in nutrition and flavour.
objectives: Compare the pasteurization schedules by time and temperature
Explain why raw milk is a public health concern

lessons.title: Time, Temperature and What Survives
lessons.objective: State the HTST and UHT time-temperature schedules, explain what each is designed to kill, and say why pasteurization is not sterilization.

lessons.title: Raw Milk and Why Regulators Object
lessons.objective: Name the pathogens associated with unpasteurized milk and state what the evidence says about the claimed benefits of raw milk.

lessons.title: Drying, Concentrating, Chilling, Freezing
lessons.objective: Compare refrigeration, freezing, evaporation, condensing and drying as preservation methods, and say what each does to water availability.

lessons.title: How Milk Goes Off
lessons.objective: Describe microbial and chemical spoilage of dairy foods, and distinguish souring from rancidity by their chemistry.

units.title: Nutrition, Labels and Regulation
units.summary: The manual asks for labeling regulations, RDA of the minerals and vitamins dairy supplies, and the consequences of going without them.
objectives: Read a Nutrition Facts label and compute a percent Daily Value
Name the deficiency disease for each nutrient dairy supplies

lessons.title: Reading the Nutrition Facts Label
lessons.objective: Identify each element of a Nutrition Facts label, compute a percent Daily Value from a serving, and explain what serving size changes.

lessons.title: RDA, DV and What the Numbers Mean
lessons.objective: Distinguish the Recommended Dietary Allowance from the Daily Value used on labels, and say who each is defined for.

lessons.title: Calcium, Vitamin D and Bone
lessons.objective: Explain why calcium and vitamin D are given together, state what dairy contributes, and name what deficiency of each causes.

lessons.title: Riboflavin, B12, Potassium and Phosphorus
lessons.objective: Name the other nutrients dairy foods supply in quantity and state a consequence of deficiency for each.

lessons.title: Whole, Low Fat, Fat Free
lessons.objective: Compare whole, reduced fat, low fat and fat free milk by fat content and by what is lost or added, including fat-soluble vitamins.

lessons.title: What 'Organic' Certifies
lessons.objective: State what organic certification requires of a dairy and what it does not claim about the resulting milk.

units.title: Lactose Intolerance, Allergy and Non-Dairy Milks
units.summary: Two different things are often confused here, and the manual names both. So do the alternatives people move to.
objectives: Distinguish an intolerance from an allergy by mechanism
Compare a plant 'milk' with dairy milk nutritionally

lessons.title: Lactose Intolerance: an Enzyme, Not an Immune Response
lessons.objective: Explain lactose intolerance as declining lactase activity, describe the symptoms and their cause, and state why it is not an allergy.

lessons.title: How Lactose Free Milk Is Made
lessons.objective: Explain how lactose free milk is produced and why it tastes sweeter than ordinary milk despite having the same total sugar mass.

lessons.title: Milk Allergy: an Immune Response to Protein
lessons.objective: Describe milk allergy as an immune reaction to casein or whey protein, name its major allergens, and state how labeling law treats milk.

lessons.title: Non-Dairy 'Milks' and What They Are Not
lessons.objective: Compare soy, almond and oat beverages with dairy milk on protein, calcium and fortification, and say which claims are equivalent.

lessons.title: What Dairy Foods Are Good For
lessons.objective: State the health contributions the evidence supports for dairy foods, and distinguish a supported claim from a marketing one.

units.title: The Lab Tasks and the Notebook
units.summary: Nine experiments are graded before the tournament starts. This unit is the measurement and experiment design they require.
objectives: Design a dairy experiment with exactly one independent variable
Compute a percentage yield against a supervisor's value

lessons.title: One Independent Variable, and Why the Rule Exists
lessons.objective: Design a dairy experiment with a single independent variable, identify the dependent and controlled variables, and explain what a second independent variable would destroy.

lessons.title: Measuring Curd Mass and Milk Fat Mass
lessons.objective: Compute a curd or butter mass as a percentage of the starting milk mass, and score it against a supervisor value the way the rules specify.

lessons.title: Temperature as a Variable You Must Hold Still
lessons.objective: Explain why the curd task specifies room temperature and the butter task about 13 degrees Celsius, and what happens to each if temperature drifts.

lessons.title: Recording Results and Naming Your Error
lessons.objective: Record an experiment so another team could repeat it, and distinguish random from systematic error in a dairy measurement.
